national.canonicalTopic: India–West Indies T20I series and Shai Hope century
national.headline: Hope’s century helps West Indies beat India and level the series
facts: In the fourth T20I in Hyderabad, West Indies scored 247/3 and India were all out for 223 in 19.3 overs; West Indies won by 24 runs.
West Indies captain Shai Hope scored 102 not out from 50 balls, his third men’s T20I century; each of his T20I hundreds was an unbeaten 102, according to the report.
The win levelled the five-match series at 2-2; the fifth T20I was scheduled for October 17 in Bengaluru.
Keemo Paul took five wickets for West Indies.
national.summary: Shai Hope’s unbeaten century and Keemo Paul’s five-wicket haul powered West Indies to a 24-run win over India, levelling the T20I series.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Fourth T20I: West Indies 247/3, India 223; West Indies won by 24 runs, with the series level at 2-2.

national.canonicalTopic: Wholesale Price Index inflation September 2026
national.headline: Wholesale inflation reached 11.4% in September 2026
facts: Wholesale price inflation was reported at 11.4% for September 2026.
Inflation in WPI food articles was 8.1%, up from 5.7% in August.
Non-food primary articles inflation was 10.3%.
The report described 11.4% as a record for the available two-and-a-half-year period of the new WPI series and a 49-month high on the longer old series.
national.summary: The September WPI reading rose sharply, with food articles and non-food primary articles both recording elevated inflation.
national.prelimsTakeaway: September 2026 WPI inflation: 11.4%; food articles inflation: 8.1%.

sources.title: Wholesale inflation rises to 49-month high of 11.4%

national.notes:

- **What:** Wholesale price inflation (**WPI**) reached **11.4%** in **September 2026**.
- **Food articles:** Inflation rose to **8.1%** from **5.7%** in **August 2026**.
- **Non-food primary articles:** Inflation of **10.3%**.

national.canonicalTopic: Supreme Court intervention concerning deleted Delhi voters
national.headline: Supreme Court indicated intervention for Delhi voters deleted during electoral-roll revision
facts: A Supreme Court Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant considered the difficulty faced by Delhi voters whose names were removed during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).
The petitioners said affected voters were being asked to make a declaration that they had never voted before when seeking restoration of their names.
The Chief Justice said the Court was considering an order to address the issue; the hearing was advanced to October 28 from October 30.
national.summary: The Supreme Court signalled that it may address the form-filing issue facing Delhi electors deleted from the rolls; the report describes an ongoing hearing, not a final ruling.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The report concerns electoral-roll inclusion procedures and an ongoing Supreme Court hearing, not a final judgment.
national.mainsAngle: Consider the balance between accurate electoral rolls, due process and protection of eligible voters’ participation.

sources.title: SC agrees to ‘take care’ of Delhi voters whose names were removed

national.notes:
# 1. Electoral-roll revision hearing
- **Court:** **Supreme Court of India**
- **Bench:** Headed by Chief Justice of India **Surya Kant**
- **Issue:** **Delhi** voters removed during the **Special Intensive Revision (SIR)** faced difficulty seeking restoration of their names.
- **Petitioners’ concern:** Affected voters were reportedly asked to declare that they had never voted before when applying for restoration.
# 2. Status and hearing
- **Status:** The Chief Justice said the Court was considering an order to address the issue; the hearing was ongoing.
- **Next hearing:** Advanced to **October 28, 2026**, from **October 30, 2026**.

> Exam angle: Test the **SIR** issue, the voter declaration dispute and the distinction between an ongoing hearing and a final ruling.

national.canonicalTopic: High-Level Committee on Demographic Changes public-input portal
national.headline: Home Ministry opens portal for public input on demographic changes
group1: Group 1 Paper III: Polity, Governance, Ethics
facts: The Ministry of Home Affairs launched a portal inviting submissions on demographic changes, preferably those observed after 2011.
The High-Level Committee on Demographic Changes is chaired by former Supreme Court judge Prakash Prabhakar Naolekar and was constituted on May 26, 2026.
The portal invites contributions from government bodies, civil society, academic and business organisations, international organisations and individuals.
The committee is to examine the nature, causes and consequences of demographic changes and recommend an operational system for identifying, detaining and deporting illegal immigrants.
national.summary: The Home Ministry’s committee portal seeks information and views on demographic change and its effects on public services, local governance, resources and social cohesion.

facts: The Union Cabinet approved ₹53,428 crore for continuation of the National Social Assistance Programme for five years, from 2026–27 to 2030–31.
The programme is to be renamed Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana.
The “Indira Gandhi” prefix is to be removed from the old-age, widow and disability pension sub-schemes.
The Cabinet also revised disability-pension eligibility criteria and assistance rates; the report does not specify the revised figures.
The article says the beneficiary base for the three pension schemes is capped at 3.09 crore.
national.summary: The Cabinet approved a five-year continuation and renaming of the social assistance programme, alongside changes to disability-pension eligibility and assistance rates.
national.staticLink: Social security pensions; National Social Assistance Programme and centrally supported welfare.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The approved outlay is ₹53,428 crore for 2026–27 to 2030–31; the renamed programme is Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana.
national.mainsAngle: Consider adequacy, beneficiary coverage and inflation adjustment in social-assistance pensions.

sources.title: ₹53,428 cr. cleared for social assistance scheme till 2030-31

national.notes:
# 1. Social assistance programme
- **Decision:** Union Cabinet approved continuation and renaming of the **National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP)**.
- **Approved amount:** **₹53,428 crore** for **five years**, from **2026–27 to 2030–31**.
- **New name:** **Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana**.
- **Sub-schemes:** The **Indira Gandhi** prefix is to be removed from the old-age, widow and disability pension sub-schemes.
# 2. Eligibility and assistance
- **Disability pension:** Eligibility criteria and assistance rates revised; revised figures were not specified in the report.
- **Beneficiary cap:** **3.09 crore** across the **three** pension schemes.
- ⚠ **Trap:** The report gives no revised disability-pension figures; do not infer them.
> Exam angle: Recall the renamed programme, approved **outlay**, continuation period and beneficiary cap.

national.canonicalTopic: Additional MGNREGA work for Forest Rights Act title holders
national.headline: No order yet on additional workdays for Forest Rights Act title holders under the new rural employment law
group1: Group 1 Paper III: Polity, Governance, Ethics
facts: The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025, guarantees 125 days of wage employment per rural household in a financial year and has no separate entitlement tier for Forest Rights Act title holders.
In an October 6, 2026 RTI reply, the Rural Development Ministry said no separate order, circular or guideline had been issued for additional workdays for FRA title holders under the new programme.
Under MGNREGA, FRA title holders had been eligible for 50 additional days beyond the usual 100-day guarantee.
For 2025–26, Andhra Pradesh had 1,70,851 households listed as eligible for 150 days of work; 36,008 availed themselves of the additional days.
national.summary: The ministry had not issued an order on whether FRA title-holder households would retain an additional 50 days under the new rural employment programme. The report also gives Andhra Pradesh’s 2025–26 uptake figures under MGNREGA.
national.staticLink: MGNREGA; Forest Rights Act, 2006; guaranteed rural wage employment.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The new law’s stated guarantee is 125 days per rural household; the article reports no separate additional-work order for FRA title holders as of October 6, 2026.
national.mainsAngle: Examine continuity of social-protection entitlements during a change in rural employment legislation, with attention to forest-dwelling communities and implementation.
national.apLink: Andhra Pradesh had 1,70,851 households eligible for 150 days under the reported 2025–26 MGNREGA data, of whom 36,008 availed the additional days.

sources.title: No order yet on extra 50 days of work for FRA title holders

national.notes:

- **Law:** **VB-G RAM G Act, 2025**
- **Guarantee:** **125 days** of wage employment per rural household in a financial year.
- **FRA title holders:** No separate entitlement tier in the new Act.
- **Ministry response:** In an **October 6, 2026** RTI reply, the **Rural Development Ministry** said no separate order, circular or guideline had been issued for additional workdays for **Forest Rights Act (FRA)** title holders.

national.canonicalTopic: Jeypore ground gecko conservation and Balda Hills mining proposal
national.headline: Mining proposal in Odisha’s Balda Hills poses a threat to the Jeypore ground gecko
group1: Group 1 Paper II: History, Culture & Geography
Group 1 Paper V: Science, Technology & Environment
facts: The Jeypore ground gecko is an endangered species of the Eastern Ghats; the report says its range includes forests in Odisha and Andhra Pradesh.
Four individuals were documented in Odisha’s Balda Hills over the past year, including one sighting in October 2026.
A proposed 147-hectare opencast bauxite mine in the Balda Hills, within Nageswari reserve forest, is identified as a threat to its habitat.
The species was first documented in 1878 and rediscovered in Odisha’s Koraput district in 2010.
national.summary: The article reports recent sightings of the endangered gecko in Odisha and warns that a proposed bauxite mine could affect its habitat in the Eastern Ghats.
national.staticLink: Eastern Ghats biodiversity; habitat protection and environmental appraisal of mining proposals.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The Jeypore ground gecko is an endangered Eastern Ghats species, rediscovered in 2010 after it had been presumed extinct for about 130 years.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss how infrastructure and mineral-development proposals should account for habitat protection and biodiversity evidence.
national.apLink: The report identifies the Jeypore ground gecko’s range as including the Eastern Ghats of Andhra Pradesh as well as Odisha; the cited mine proposal is in Odisha.

national.canonicalTopic: Supreme Court safeguards on communication of arrest grounds
national.headline: Supreme Court sets requirements for communicating grounds of arrest and re-arrest
facts: In Jaskaran Jeet Singh Deol v. State of Punjab (September 2026), the Supreme Court said an investigating agency seeking to re-arrest an accused after an earlier arrest was held illegal for failure to provide written grounds must obtain the magistrate’s permission.
The application must explain why the grounds were not supplied, be made after those grounds have been furnished to the accused, and carry the immediate superior authority’s endorsement.
The Court called for the investigation to be transferred to another officer and for a departmental inquiry into the investigating officer’s lapse.

The article reports that the Court required grounds of arrest to be communicated in writing, in a language understood by the accused, at least two hours before remand proceedings; non-compliance renders the arrest and remand illegal.
national.summary: The Supreme Court’s ruling addresses communication of arrest grounds and the consequences of failing to meet that safeguard, including the procedure for a subsequent re-arrest.
national.staticLink: Article 22 of the Constitution; Section 47 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Article 22 protects an arrested person’s rights; the article identifies Section 47 of the BNSS as the statutory duty to communicate grounds of arrest.
national.mainsAngle: Examine how procedural safeguards at arrest protect personal liberty and what institutional accountability should follow their breach.

sources.title: How has the SC strengthened arrest safeguards?

national.notes:
# 1. Communicating grounds of arrest
- **Case:** **Jaskaran Jeet Singh Deol v. State of Punjab**, **September 2026**.
- **Court:** **Supreme Court of India**.
- **Requirement:** Grounds of arrest must be communicated in writing, in a language understood by the accused, at least **two hours** before remand proceedings.
- **Consequence:** Non-compliance renders the arrest and remand illegal.
- **Legal basis cited:** **Article 22** of the Constitution; **Section 47** of the **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS)**.
# 2. Procedure for re-arrest
- **Permission:** If an earlier arrest was held illegal because written grounds were not provided, the investigating agency must obtain the magistrate’s permission to re-arrest.
- **Application requirements:** Explain why the grounds were not supplied; be made after the grounds have been furnished to the accused; carry the immediate superior authority’s endorsement.
- **Further directions:** Transfer the investigation to another officer and hold a departmental inquiry into the investigating officer’s lapse.
> Exam angle: Test the written-grounds safeguard, **two-hour** timing and magistrate-permission requirements for re-arrest.

andhraPradesh.headline: Vijayawada to host National SARAS Mela
facts: The National Sale of Articles of Rural Artisans Society (SARAS) Mela was scheduled at Punnami Ghat, Vijayawada, as part of the Dasara programme.
The event was organised under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods Mission, with the Ministry of Rural Development and Andhra Pradesh government involved.
The report said more than 600 stalls were set up and participation had risen to over 1,500 women, chiefly from Self-Help Groups.
The mela was scheduled for inauguration by President Droupadi Murmu on October 15, 2026.
andhraPradesh.summary: The Vijayawada SARAS Mela brought rural-artisan and Self-Help Group products to a national exhibition supported by the rural livelihoods mission.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: SARAS Mela: rural-artisan exhibition associated with DAY-NRLM; reported venue: Punnami Ghat, Vijayawada.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Discuss how SHG-linked markets and public exhibitions can expand livelihoods, market access and women’s economic participation.
andhraPradesh.apLink: The reported SARAS Mela venue was Punnami Ghat in Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh.

sources.title: In a first, Vijayawada to host National SARAS Mela

andhraPradesh.notes:
# 1. Mela and venue
- **Event:** National Sale of Articles of Rural Artisans Society (**SARAS**) Mela
- **Venue:** **Punnami Ghat, Vijayawada**, **Andhra Pradesh**
- **Occasion:** Part of the **Dasara** programme
- **Status:** Scheduled; inauguration was scheduled for **October 15, 2026**
# 2. Mission and participants
- **Mission:** **Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM)**
- **Ministry:** **Ministry of Rural Development**; **Andhra Pradesh government** also involved
- **Stalls:** More than **600**
- **Women participants:** Over **1,500**, chiefly from **Self-Help Groups (SHGs)**
- **Scheduled inaugurator:** President **Droupadi Murmu**
- ⚠ **Trap:** The report said the President was scheduled to inaugurate the mela; do not treat that as confirmation that the inauguration had occurred
> Exam angle: Identify the **SARAS Mela’s** venue, DAY-NRLM association and scheduled inaugurator.
